title: A Hand That Pinches: Stroke, Force, Friction, and How Heavy a Thing Two Fingers Can Hold

questions.question: What holds a thing between two fingers?
options: The squeeze, which presses the thing against gravity
The fingers' stiffness, which wedges it in place
The shape of the pads, which hooks under it
Friction at the pads, which the squeeze makes
questions.explanation: The squeeze is horizontal and the weight is vertical, so the squeeze cannot carry the weight itself. What it does is make friction at each pad, up to mu times the squeeze.

questions.question: A kilogram at rest needed what squeeze at a friction of 0.5?
options: 4.9 N, since two pads share it
19.6 N, the weight over the friction
235 N, the most the hand can give
questions.explanation: Two pads give twice mu times the squeeze, and that must equal the weight: 9.81 N over 2 times 0.5 is 9.81 N.

questions.question: Lifting it at 5 m/s2 needed:
options: 9.81 N, the same: friction does not depend on speed
19.6 N, twice as much
4.81 N, only the extra
questions.explanation: The hand has to supply the mass times g plus the acceleration. 1 kg times 14.81 m/s2 over 2 times 0.5 is 14.81 N.

questions.question: Pads at half the friction hold:
options: 16.0 kg, the same, if the squeeze is doubled
4.0 kg against 16.0 kg
8.0 kg against 16.0 kg
12.0 kg against 16.0 kg
questions.explanation: The heaviest mass is proportional to the friction. At full squeeze and a safety factor of 1.5 that was 16.0 kg, and 8.0 kg on wet or oily pads.

questions.question: Why does a safety factor go on the force?
options: Friction and the acceleration are not known exactly
The motor gives less force as it warms
The stroke is not known exactly
A larger force closes the hand sooner
questions.explanation: The formula is exact for numbers that are not. A dirty pad has less friction than the one written down, and the arm may accelerate harder than planned.

questions.question: What is the closing time of a hand a part of?
options: The safety factor
The heaviest mass it holds
Every pick's cycle time
The friction of the pads
questions.explanation: Closing takes the distance the fingers travel over their speed, and it is paid on every pick and again on every release.
